Defensive core against beatdown (clock 0:54-0:37): Tesla first, Fire Spirit to keep the Magic Archer alive, Royal Delivery on the Baby Dragon, Ronin on the Mini P.E.K.K.A. — "Dude, this deck's defense is just so powerful, man." (t=143)

Why he thinks the deck is broken (t=48-53, t=149-154): "Everyone hates the Ronin so much who plays with any type of melee unit because it just gets completely decimated" and "this might be the craziest new card I've seen yet, man. It just hard counters specific decks way too hard." Result: win over a Golem / Battle Healer / Elixir Collector beatdown player — "Easy first win though." (t=154)

new_deck.rationale: Goblin Barrel, Wall Breakers, Skeletons and Fire Spirit all die to the same small spells, so whichever one the opponent cannot answer connects, and a 2.9-elixir average lets him replay it before their answer cycles back.
new_deck.why_it_works_md: The deck pairs four small-spell-bait threats (Goblin Barrel, Evo Wall Breakers, Skeletons, Fire Spirit) with a defence that costs almost nothing to hold: Tesla for air and building-targeters, Royal Delivery for clumped air support, and the Ronin, whose parry deflects 200% of a melee attacker's own hit. Against any deck whose best defensive DPS is a melee troop the Ronin effectively removes the answer — "his best DPS unit is the Mini Pekka, but of course, the Mini Pekka just one shots itself" — so the barrels and Wall Breakers keep connecting for free. Ryley plays the Ronin on his own half as the anchor and only pushes it near the bridge to deny a heavy opponent the free back-tank placement, then closes with a Hero Magic Archer at the bridge once a tower is low. Ryley describes it as a revision of an earlier Cannon-based list, with Tesla and Royal Delivery added specifically because the older version "was quite a bit weak to air units".
